title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors to look beyond governance structures and judge how a board really works: its information, decisions, culture and challenge, and the evidence needed to reach a sound supervisory conclusion.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical method for assessing board dynamics and decision-making, not just board composition and terms of reference. Participants leave able to read board papers and minutes critically, test the quality of decisions and challenge, plan and conduct board-level interviews, and draw evidence-based conclusions.
sections.What It Covers: How the board works in practice, agendas, papers and information quality, information asymmetry and side conversations, oversight versus micromanagement, judging decision quality, culture, challenge and psychological safety, groupthink, board personalities, evaluation, succession, skills and AI in the boardroom, and case-study interviews.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and governance specialists who assess boards and senior management of regulated firms
Staff conducting fit and proper, governance or culture reviews and interviewing chairs and directors
Senior supervisors and team leaders who review governance assessments and decide the supervisory response
Learning Objectives: Explain why sound governance structures can coexist with ineffective board dynamics
Assess agendas, board papers and management information for quality and real decision support
Evaluate the quality of board decisions by testing the process rather than the outcome
Identify signs of weak challenge, low psychological safety and groupthink
Plan and conduct evidence-led interviews with chairs, directors and executives
Reach and evidence a supervisory conclusion on board effectiveness and the appropriate response
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short input with analysis of board packs and minutes, group exercises and role-play interviews, ending in a case-study interview workshop, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's governance framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of governance assessment or supervisory interviews is helpful. No board experience is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)

modules.title: Beyond Structures: Why Board Dynamics Matter
modules.summary: Why a governance assessment can confirm the right structures and still miss how the board actually works, and the supervisor's framework for assessing dynamics systematically.
objectives: Distinguish governance form from governance substance
Apply the supervisor's eye: look for, concerns, evidence, questions and conclusion
Identify the evidence sources available for assessing board dynamics
syllabus: Composition, committees and policies versus behaviour and challenge
How weak board dynamics have contributed to firm failures
Evidence sources: packs, minutes, evaluations, observation and interviews
The five questions of the supervisor's eye

modules.title: Agendas, Board Papers and Information Quality
modules.summary: How the agenda, the quality of papers and the volume of information shape what the board actually scrutinises, and what good and poor board information look like.
objectives: Assess whether the agenda gives proper time to strategic and risk issues
Distinguish a decision-ready board paper from narrative without a clear ask
Evaluate whether management information is concise, prioritised and exception-based
syllabus: Agenda curation, routine reporting and items carried over or pushed to the end
Good papers: decision required, options, recommendation, risks and prior challenge
Information overload and the shortcuts overwhelmed boards take
Supervisory questions to test papers and information quality

modules.title: Information Asymmetry and the Line Between Oversight and Management
modules.summary: How boards manage the gap between what they know and what management knows, how decisions get made before the meeting, and where oversight ends and micromanagement begins.
objectives: Assess how the board validates information and uses independent assurance
Recognise when the board meeting has become a ratification exercise
Judge whether the board is under-engaged, appropriately engaged or micromanaging
syllabus: Independent assurance: internal and external audit, risk function and outside experts
Pre-meetings and side conversations: legitimate preparation or foregone conclusion
Reading minutes for recorded debate and challenge
Oversight versus direction of day-to-day decisions and staff

modules.title: Judging the Quality of Board Decisions
modules.summary: How to test a significant board decision on the strength of its process rather than its outcome, and how to tell whether a board learns from its own history.
objectives: Apply a structured test of why, why now, alternatives, assumptions and downside
Assess whether success measures and the recorded rationale are adequate
Evaluate whether the board revisits decisions and learns from experience
syllabus: Process versus outcome: good decisions that go wrong and vice versa
Alternatives, key assumptions and the worst case
Success measures and minutes that record why, not just what
Look-back reviews, repeat findings and organisational learning

modules.title: Culture, Challenge and Psychological Safety
modules.summary: How board culture shows itself in meetings, minutes and interviews, the role of the chair in enabling challenge, and how to tell effective challenge from confrontation or avoidance.
objectives: Explain why challenge depends on psychological safety
Read the signs of board culture: airtime, silence, interruptions and openness
Assess the effectiveness of the chair in enabling challenge
syllabus: Psychological safety and how its absence shows up
Observable signs of culture in meetings and minutes
Effective and ineffective chairs
Challenge, confrontation and avoiding conflict to keep the peace

modules.title: Groupthink and Board Personalities
modules.summary: Why some boards drift into consensus at the expense of realistic appraisal, the warning signs, and how recognising common board personalities helps plan interviews without prejudging findings.
objectives: Identify the conditions and warning signs of groupthink
Assess the countermeasures a board uses to protect independent judgement
Use board personality types as an interview planning aid, not a finding
syllabus: Risk factors: long tenure, social closeness and a dominant chair or chief executive
Warning signs: quick unanimity, self-censorship and private doubts
Countermeasures: devil's advocate, anonymous polling, 'what would change our mind?'
The dominator, silent director, absentee, box-ticker and permanent devil's advocate

modules.title: Keeping the Board Effective: Evaluation, Succession, Skills and AI
modules.summary: The mechanisms a board uses to stay effective over time, what good practice looks like in each, and the emerging question of how AI is used in matters that come to the board.
objectives: Assess the quality and follow-through of board evaluations
Evaluate succession planning and the use of a skills matrix
Identify how reliance on AI in board decision-making is governed and assured
syllabus: Internal and external board evaluation and tracking actions to completion
Succession for the chair, independent directors and key executives
Skills matrices, capability gaps and appointments on relationships
AI in the boardroom: validation, accountability and model limits

modules.title: Case-Study Interview Workshop
modules.summary: A practical workshop in which participants plan and conduct interviews with the board of a case-study firm, test real board decisions and reach an evidenced supervisory conclusion.
objectives: Plan an interview strategy and question set for the chair, directors and executives
Test whether the board, rather than a shareholder or management, owned key decisions
Formulate a supervisory conclusion on board effectiveness and the response
syllabus: Testing an optimistic business plan and an intra-group outsourcing decision
A board's response to a breach of its own risk appetite limit
Role-play interviews with feedback on questioning and evidence
Workshop: findings, rating and proposed supervisory response

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: How Financial Firms Work: Business Models and Financial Statements for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping supervisors understand how financial firms make money, read their accounts and identify capital, liquidity and business model risks.

related.title: Supervising Compliance in Practice: Masterclass Series
related.summary: Ten half-day masterclasses showing supervisors how to test whether firms' compliance arrangements work in practice across core compliance areas.

related.title: Supervisory Risk Assessment Toolkit
related.summary: A ten-module toolkit taking supervisors through the full firm risk assessment cycle, from business model and governance analysis to panels, risk ratings and findings.

related.title: Foundations of Financial Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module induction for new regulatory staff covering why we regulate, the authority's powers, risk-based supervision and a first supervisory case.

related.title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.
